Algebra 2 · Unit 4: Quadratic Functions

Complex Solutions

Find and interpret complex solutions of quadratic equations.

What you’ll learn

  • Find complex solutions with the quadratic formula
  • Recognize conjugate pairs
  • Explain what complex roots mean for a graph

The mountain biking connection

Ask when a jump reaches a height it never gets to: the equation still has solutions, they’re just complex.

Learning activities

Interactive lab · from Algebra 2: Solving Equations and Modeling Constraints

Race-Day Workshop

Join an enduro team’s technical crew: check suspension sag with formulas and absolute value, work out the speed a stage needs with rational equations, and survey a climb with a radical equation, then pass the Race-Day Certification.

Level
Intermediate to Advanced
Time
20-25 min
  • 3 missions
  • Sag calculator and tolerance gauge
  • Race clock simulator
  • Trail survey simulator
  • Algebra debugger
  • Race-Day Certification (6)
  • Optional complex-number extension

Practices here: Explain what complex roots mean for a graph

Interactive lab · from Algebra 2: Quadratic Graphs

Trail Dynamics Lab

Model stopping distance as a quadratic and solve it backwards, rebuild a jump in standard, vertex and factored form, then find landing heights with square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and the discriminant, all the way to complex roots.

Level
Intermediate to Advanced
Time
20-25 min
  • 3 missions
  • Stopping distance simulator
  • Jump equation decoder and tuner
  • Trajectory height analyzer
  • Final Course Analysis (12)
  • Optional complex-number practice

Practices here: Find complex solutions with the quadratic formula; Recognize conjugate pairs; Explain what complex roots mean for a graph

Launch lab → Trail Dynamics Lab

Interactive lab · from Algebra 2: Polynomial Graphs

Pump Track Profile Lab

Decode a pump track profile’s degree, end behavior and turning points, combine and expand polynomial profiles, find zeros and multiplicity with the Rational Zero Theorem, then divide it apart with synthetic and long division and the Remainder and Factor Theorems.

Level
Intermediate to Advanced
Time
25-30 min
  • 4 missions
  • Flow line decoder
  • Expansion workbench and factor builder
  • Synthetic division console
  • Final Track Analysis (12)
  • Optional complex-zeros extension

Practices here: Recognize conjugate pairs
